title: Accessible interaction patterns
learningObjectives: Explain accessible interaction patterns and implement reliable browser event and network workflows.

understand.concept: Accessible interaction patterns use semantic controls, keyboard support, visible focus, predictable activation, and correctly exposed state. Custom widgets should follow established interaction patterns and use ARIA only when native semantics are insufficient.
understand.whyItMatters: A control that only works with a pointer excludes keyboard users and may fail with assistive technology. Native elements reduce custom work.
understand.analogy: An accessible control offers more than a visible handle: it offers a usable path for different input methods.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript scheduling, HTTP semantics, and browser security follow platform standards.

explain.narrative: The native button supports keyboard activation and its aria-expanded state stays in sync with the panel visibility.

practise.guidedTask: Build a disclosure control and test Tab, Enter, Space, focus visibility, and state announcements.
practise.independentTask: Build an asynchronous feature with explicit states, cancellation, and error handling. Document which failures are safe to retry.
hints: Separate HTTP errors from network and parsing errors.
Use bounded retries only for suitable operations.
Tie UI updates to the latest active request.
